### Who was Rabindranath Tagore?

Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a Bengali poet, educator, and thinker—the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature (1913). He founded Visva-Bharati to embody cosmopolitan learning rooted in Indian traditions. Essays and lectures address nationalism, freedom, and the religion of man. Handbook dates: 1861–1941. Dialogue with Gandhi and travels in Asia and the West made him a global intellectual.

### Major ideas

Creative freedom and personality unfold in relation to an infinite that exceeds nation-state idols. Nationalism can become a predatory abstraction against the living human. Education should awaken curiosity and artistic sympathy, not drill alone. The religion of man seeks spiritual unity without sectarian hatred. East–West encounter should be mutual hospitality, not domination. Poetry and song are modes of philosophical disclosure.

### Major works

-   Gitanjali
-   Nationalism
-   The Religion of Man
-   Sadhana

### Legacy

Tagore shaped modern Indian letters, comparative education, and critiques of chauvinist nationalism. His songs include India’s and Bangladesh’s national anthems. Philosophers of cosmopolitanism continually reread his lectures.
